subject: Post-demo: retrieval stress scenarios, reranker comparison & prompt suite
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: retrieval stress scenarios, reranker comparison & prompt suite

Thanks again for the session this morning — appreciated the candid discussion on documents, latency targets, and edge-case behaviour. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

High-level takeaways
- Primary goal: improve answer grounding for enterprise manuals while keeping p95 latency <= 350ms for user-facing queries.
- Data surface: ~1.2M short docs + 80k long PDFs (indexing strategy matters).
- Current infra: Aegis uses Pinecone for embeddings, live index replication across us-east/us-west.

Initial technical recommendations (RAG-specific)
1) Retriever config to exercise in the pilot
   - Dense retrieval (faiss-hnsw) with 1536-d embeddings, top_k=100, then rerank top_10
   - Add a metadata filter on doc_type and source when available to reduce spurious matches
2) Reranker options to A/B in pilot
   - Cross-encoder (re-ranker-large): highest grounding precision, higher CPU latency (~45-120ms per-query)
   - Lightweight bi-encoder + asymmetric rerank (bi-encoder to prune, cheap cross-encoder only on top-4): best cost/latency tradeoff
3) Grounding metrics we should measure
   - Grounding precision@1/3/5 (human-annotated), hallucination rate (binary), citation accuracy (doc id + span), and recall on known-answer probes
   - Operational metrics: embedding P95 embed latency, retriever recall@k, reranker CPU time, end-to-end p95
4) Stress scenarios to include in eval suite
   - Long-context queries (user pastes 8–12 pages), partial matches where label text is paraphrased, cold-start documents added between runs

Model fit notes
- Recommendation: try two model families for generation + reranker stack: redwood-3b-llm-quant (fast, cheaper, slightly more prone to omission) and redwood-7b-instruct (higher fidelity; use as fallback for hallucination-sensitive flows).
- Use a fixed prompt-suite (attached) with explicit citation templates to reduce free-form answers.

Attachments + artifacts
- raggap_benchmarks.csv (sample benchmark rows from today's demo)
- prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (starter prompts for user-facing and system probes)
- link to shared Drive with eval harness and sample labels: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bRagBenchmarks

Next steps / asks (ownership + ETA)
- Aegis: confirm which index replica (us-east/us-west/both) we'll use for pilot by EOD Fri — action Tom.
- Redwood (Ben): we'll spin up two reranker configs and run the following probe suite (recall, grounding precision, latency) — deliver results within 5 business days.
- Redwood (Neha): schedule a 30-min sync one week after results to decide pilot rollout and SLA targets.

Thanks — I pasted the prompt-suite and benchmark csv into Drive. If you want, we can also sample-run a few of your real user queries this week (needs an NDA scope exception).

– Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: raggap_benchmarks.csv (CSV), prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (JSONL)

Tom — quick answers and proposed measurement plan.

Reranker latency guidance
- The 45-120ms band is per pair for a medium cross-encoder on a single CPU core; when you run top_10 rerank that translates to ~450–1200ms if you do naive cross-encoder on all 10 pairs (unacceptable for your SLA).
- Our pragmatic approach: bi-encoder prune to top_20 (GPU-backed, ~40ms), then cross-encode top_4 (CPU or GPU hybrid) — expected p95 contribution ~80–180ms depending on infra. We'll measure both.

Measurement plan (what we'll run)
- Two configs: (A) full cross-encoder rerank top_10, (B) prune-then-rerank (bi-encoder -> cross top_4).
- Benchmarks: grounding precision@1/3/5 (human eval on 500 probes), citation accuracy (span-level), hallucination rate (binary), end-to-end p50/p95, cost per 1k queries.
- Stress scenarios: long-context synthetic (8–12 page), incremental document absorbs (cold-start add 10k docs), paraphrase-resistance set.

I'll attach the short measurement spec and reranker-metrics template. We'll provision test instances and post results to the Drive link.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
